subsystems.name: Recording front end
subsystems.role: senses the electrical spikes of individual neurons.
parts: penetrating microelectrode arrays or flexible threads

subsystems.name: Stimulation front end
subsystems.role: writes activity back into tissue by driving neurons to fire in a chosen pattern.
parts: light emitters if the cells have been made light-sensitive

subsystems.name: Local mesh nodes
subsystems.role: the hypothetical micron-scale devices that would sit beside synapses and translate chemistry to data.

subsystems.name: Power and data link
subsystems.role: feeds power to thousands of nodes deep in tissue and carries their data out.

subsystems.name: Neural codec
subsystems.role: software that translates spike patterns into meaning and back.

buildSteps.title: Record from many neurons at once
buildSteps.detail: Arrays of electrodes or thread-like probes are placed in a brain region and their signals amplified and sorted into individual neurons' spikes.

buildSteps.title: Find what the activity means
buildSteps.detail: Recordings are matched against what the animal or person is doing or seeing, so a decoder can guess intent from firing patterns. This is straightforward for arm movement, weak for language, and unsolved for abstract knowledge.

buildSteps.title: Write activity back
buildSteps.detail: The same electrodes, or light delivered to genetically modified cells, are used to make chosen neurons fire — closing the loop within one brain.

buildSteps.title: Shrink the interface
buildSteps.detail: To reach millions of neurons rather than hundreds, the alternative is thousands of free-floating microscale nodes. Closest precedent is 'neural dust': millimetre-scale devices that were powered and read by ultrasound in a rat's peripheral nerve. Nothing comparable yet works inside a brain, and no design exists at true nanometre scale.

buildSteps.title: Link two brains
buildSteps.detail: A decoder in one brain is wired to a stimulator in another, so activity in the sender produces a signal the receiver perceives. This has been done at the level of a single motor decision; it is not thought transfer.

buildSteps.title: Scale the channel count
buildSteps.detail: Bandwidth must rise from roughly a thousand channels to millions, with the tissue surviving years of implantation.

buildSteps.title: Handle memory specifically
buildSteps.detail: Memory is stored as distributed changes in synapses, not as a file. Researchers can reactivate a mouse's fear memory by stimulating the cells that were active during learning, but there is no known way to read out a specific memory and write it into a different brain.

buildSteps.title: Add the network
buildSteps.detail: Finally, routing, synchronisation, identity and consent layers would turn pair links into a mesh — a systems-engineering problem on top of an unsolved neuroscience one.

prerequisites.why: implants with about a thousand electrodes are in early human trials, but long-term stability and immune response remain unsolved.

prerequisites.tech: A readable neural code for concepts and memories
prerequisites.why: without it there is nothing to transmit; only simple motor and sensory signals have been decoded.

prerequisites.tech: Microscale devices that survive inside the brain
prerequisites.why: power, data, biocompatibility and the sheer number of nodes required have no working solution.
demonstrated in the 2010s for single motor decisions between people and between animals using EEG and magnetic stimulation.
optogenetics works in animals but requires genetic modification; electrical stimulation cannot target cell types.

pathway.milestone: single-bit brain-to-brain links and early human implants with around a thousand electrodes
pathway.unlocks: proof that signals can be passed between nervous systems at all.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional implants that read and write thousands of neurons stably for years
pathway.unlocks: usable motor and speech prosthetics, and the first two-way links between people.

pathway.milestone: mesoscale recording across many brain regions and better theories of what the activity encodes
pathway.unlocks: transmission of richer signals, such as images or simple intentions, over a network.

pathway.milestone: millions of wireless microscale nodes operating inside a living brain
pathway.unlocks: the hardware a mesh would need — still without a known method for transferring a memory.

pathway.milestone: a shared neural code that can be decoded in one person and re-encoded in another
pathway.unlocks: the tile's promise of knowledge, memory and emotion transfer, which currently has no basis in known neuroscience.
